overall: Atlanta had a hotter-than-expected day, with temperatures surging to a running max of 91.4°F in the early-to-mid afternoon before a severe thunderstorm complex caused a dramatic drop — from ~89.6°F at 16:52 ET to 80.6°F by 17:52 ET, nearly a 9°F plunge in one hour. As of 20:49 ET the current temp is 80.6°F and falling at roughly 1.8°F/hr, with active severe thunderstorm warnings and a watch in effect through 11 PM for the metro region.
forecast_obs_notes: All three NWP models significantly underforecast today's actual peak — ECMWF (87.5°F), NBM (86.8°F), and even the warmest guidance, HRRR (90.1°F), all came in below the observed running max of 91.4°F. The INTRADAY model, anchored to the locked-in running max, correctly concentrates 96.8% of probability in the 90–91°F bucket, while the META model assigns residual probability to 92–95°F buckets that are now physically unreachable given the storm-driven cooling underway.
max_temp_prediction: Today's TMAX is effectively locked in at 91.4°F. The day peaked around 16:19 ET (over 4.5 hours ago), the give-up classifier fired at hour 14.67 with 91% confidence, and ongoing severe thunderstorm activity has already driven temperatures 11°F below the daily high with no possibility of recovery at this hour. Confidence is very high — this is essentially a confirmed observation, not a forecast.
